feedback.trigger: An approved implementation task changes an architecture boundary.
feedback.actual_behavior: Execution starts from the SOW file list without checking that the selected design conforms to project authority.
feedback.expected_behavior: Re-check authority mapping and planned evidence before implementation, then stop on conflict or ambiguity.
feedback.invariant: Execution preserves project-declared architecture instead of optimizing around it.

scenarios.context: The SOW identifies the governing architecture invariant and verification evidence.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Confirm the mapping, implement within it, and verify the stated evidence.
scenarios.must_not: Introduce a second ownership path for implementation convenience.

scenarios.request: Apply an approved text-only documentation correction.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Execute the docs change without demanding architecture evidence.
scenarios.must_not: Block a non-design edit on an irrelevant audit.

scenarios.request: Implement a SOW whose selected design conflicts with a newer project authority document.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Stop and route back for a project-authority amendment or revised SOW.

feedback.trigger: An approved task requires reading and navigating a repository.
feedback.actual_behavior: Execution invokes a separate search-policy skill and treats CodeGraph as mandatory before normal inspection.
feedback.expected_behavior: Choose any available method that gathers sufficient code evidence without requiring CodeGraph setup or invocation.
feedback.invariant: Execution requires real repository evidence, not one mandatory code-navigation tool.

scenarios.request: Implement an approved change after inspecting the relevant code paths.
scenarios.context: CodeGraph is unavailable, while direct reads and text search can establish the implementation shape.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Inspect with available tools and continue once evidence is sufficient.
scenarios.must_not: Initialize or invoke CodeGraph merely because the task touches code.

scenarios.request: Analyze the caller impact of a known symbol using the already-available semantic graph.
scenarios.context: CodeGraph is initialized and is the cheapest reliable tool for the question.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Use CodeGraph when it is useful without treating it as globally required.
scenarios.must_not: Ban CodeGraph or force a less suitable tool.

scenarios.request: Inspect an unfamiliar repository where no single search tool answers the full question.
scenarios.context: Several available methods provide complementary evidence.
scenarios.expected_behavior: Combine suitable methods proportionally to the uncertainty.
scenarios.must_not: Replace CodeGraph-first with another universal mandatory search order.
